mechanics.fact: Free-return loop around the far side out to 252,756 miles, then home
mechanics.mechanic: Crater sink-and-rise topology at gravity 240: drop off the launch rim, sink into the shadowed far-side crater, drop-bonk the Integrity Sprites off the crater floors up to the far rim, then ride the return ledges home; the loop is flown as a plunge, a bonk-rise, and a falling return

mechanics.fact: Re-entry near 25,000 mph heated the shield toward 5,000F, then slowed to 20 mph for splashdown
mechanics.mechanic: Plasma drip rain and a crusher crowd the return ledges, then the route falls a vertical splashdown well between staggered heat lasers into the low basin; the crown is taken on foot past the basin roller, with no bounce in the last 900px

mechanics.fact: Far-side eclipse and solar exposure on the lunar arc
mechanics.mechanic: Timed cosmic-ray particle streams sweep the high arc decks, with a laser gate at the arc throat

mechanics.fact: Four crew rode Orion Integrity; recovery waited at splashdown
mechanics.mechanic: Two rescue cages ride the arc and basin perches as the crew/recovery markers, with checkpoints as flight milestones (translunar injection, far side, entry interface)
